Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 68, verse 1:

Nun. By the pen and what they write.

Here Allah swears by the letter Nun, by the pen (qalam) and by writing (kitabat). The letter Nun is a unique letter, and the connection between it and the pen and writing is clear. Why has He sworn by these things? Because in Islam great importance has been given to reading and writing. The purpose of this guidance is that you should give attention to this task, for the Arabs were unlettered (ummi) and were not inclined towards reading and writing. Very few people among the Arabs knew how to read and write, whereas the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ) was to play an important role among the humankind to come, and for that, reading and writing were very necessary. The spread of reading and writing was a fundamental point of Islamic policy, so that this doctrine and the system that was to be established upon it could be spread throughout the world, and so that this Ummah could lead humanity. There is no doubt that for this purpose, reading and writing were a basic necessity.

This point is also confirmed by the fact that the beginning of revelation was as follows:

﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created, created man from a clot of blood. Read, and your Lord is most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know.﴾ (96:1-5) The Prophet, who was unlettered, was commanded to read, and Allah had decided that he would be unlettered, and there was considerable wisdom in that. But when the revelation came, it came with the guidance to read and to write. Here, through the letter Nun, this was further emphasised, and an oath was taken by the pen and by the lines. This was a method of training this Ummah, which was to play a great role in this universe.

In short, here the oath is by the alphabetic letter Nun, then by the pen, and then by the lines (of writing). The purpose is to show that recitation and writing are a fundamental and very important policy of Islam.

Second, to refute the accusation the disbelievers were making, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was possessed (majnun), Allah here declares that by the grace and favour of your Lord you are not majnun.

﴿Ma anta bi-ni'mati rabbika bi-majnun﴾ "You are not, by the favour of your Lord, a madman." In a short verse, one matter is affirmed and one is negated. What is affirmed is that you have the grace and favour of Allah upon you; what is negated is that you are majnun. And the affirmation of mercy is made with extraordinary tenderness.

Rabbika: that is, by the grace and favour of your Lord.

When a person reads the events of the Prophet's life before prophethood, he is astonished that these people level such an accusation against a man whom they knew to be a very wise person. Several years before prophethood, when they disagreed over placing the Black Stone, you resolved the matter with great wisdom. Then they gave you the title al-Amin (the Trustworthy), and they used to keep their trusts with you. Until the time of the Hijrah, trusts were kept with you. Even in a state of bitter enmity, they had confidence in you. Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, stayed in Makkah for a period after the Hijrah so that he could hand over the people's trusts that had been left with you to their rightful owners. Moreover, these were the very people who had never heard a lie from the blessed tongue of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan, "Before he claimed prophethood, did you ever accuse him of lying?" Abu Sufyan, though he was a fierce enemy of his, said, "No." Upon this, Heraclius said: "One who does not tell lies about people would not tell lies about Allah, so that he would speak the truth to people and lie about Allah."

A person is amazed that the people of Makkah dared to say this and similar things about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, although you were renowned among them for lofty character, kindness, truthfulness, and great wisdom. But love and hatred blind and deafen a person, and a person becomes ready to tell lies for his own purposes, and everyone knows that the speaker is a liar.

﴿Ma anta bi-ni'mati rabbika bi-majnun﴾ "You are not, by the favour of your Lord, a madman." Thus, with great affection and sympathy, this accusation is negated from you, you are declared honourably cleared of it, and their disbelieving enmity and shameful accusation are rejected.

And indeed, for you there is a reward that will never end. That is, there is for you a lasting and continuous reward; this flow will never be cut off, nor will it reach an end. Your Lord has bestowed prophethood upon you, and this is a very great honour. This is a very great and genuine consolation, and it is extremely complete. After this, a person does not care about any deprivation, any oppression, or any slander. When the Lord, Exalted is He, says that there is for you such a continuous reward, whose flow will not be cut off, then it is obvious that a person then does not care about any difficulty that comes in this path, especially when this assurance comes from the Lord with intimacy and with honour and dignity.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 68, verse 4:

After this, a great testimony comes in the Prophet's favour. This is a very great honour.

﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous (standard of) character.﴾ (68:4) Upon the Prophet ﷺ, the entire universe joins in this praise and commendation, and within the very spirit of this entire universe it is established that you were the possessor of a great character.

No pen has the power to describe your virtues, and no person has the power to conceive of your character or to explain this great certificate. These great words come from the Great Lord, and the Lord Most High can explain His own great testimony. What are the standards of greatness with Allah, and how great His servant is, only He knows, the One who said:

﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous (standard of) character.﴾ (68:4) This great character is something that no human can conceive of with his limited intellect and perception. Yet, from various aspects, your character was "great."

The first aspect is that this statement is coming from Allah. The Lord Most High is bestowing upon you the title of "great character." This includes Allah's creation and His boundless universe. All the angelic beings of the higher realm (mala' a'la), who are the agents of the Lord's universe, are all included in it.

One aspect of your great character is that you received this divine testimony. You received it from your Lord, knowing that the Great Lord of this great universe is saying, "This is a very great honour." These words have a great meaning, a breadth, and a lofty resonance. You knew of what Great Being this testimony was, and how great this testimony is.

It was the capacity of Muhammad ﷺ alone that was able to accept this great testimony. Only he had the fortitude to receive this testimony from this great source and to remain steadfast and serious in his place and station, and to bear the pressure and impact of this great testimony. It was a praise, yet no movement or agitation arose within his being. With complete tranquillity, complete balance, and seriousness, you accepted this honour. And the great proof of your greatness is that you took up the burden of this great address.

The books of the Seerah are filled with narrations of your great character. Your Companions speak eloquently on this subject, and your own conduct is itself a great testimony to this. But the great honour from the Lord is greater still. It comes from the Most High, the Great, the Exalted Lord. And even greater than this is that, having received this great testimony from the Creator of the universe, you remained serious, composed, firm, and steadfast in your station. You did not display your superiority over people, you did not adopt loftiness, you did not adopt grandeur, and you absorbed it, and your humility remained as it was. Although this was a very great honour.

Allah knows whom He is making a messenger. Despite your greatness, Muhammad ﷺ was a Messenger, and despite this cosmic greatness, he was bearing the responsibilities of prophethood and presenting, before the people, a model of greatness of character as a human being.

The perfection and beauty of this final Messenger, the magnitude and comprehensiveness of it, and its truth and sincerity, could only be borne by the one whom the Creator of the universe had addressed with the title: "you are of a tremendous character." And then You (the Prophet) were also given the strength to receive this greatness, and to remain balanced and serious, and to remain composed like a great human being. Only a great person can bear the greatness that has been given in these words. After this great praise and commendation, the Qur'an at times also contains reproach directed at you, but you heard that too with great dignity, with complete balance and tranquillity, just as the proclamation of this greatness came to you. In the same way, verses warning you have also been given a place in this everlasting Book. Allah has concealed nothing, and in both circumstances the Final Prophet remained great. You received both matters with greatness.

The reality of the Muhammadan self lies hidden within the Muhammadan message, and the measure of Muhammad's greatness is the greatness of the Muhammadan message. And the Muhammadan reality is, like the reality of the religion of Islam, as far from human perception and human observation as a galaxy is far away in this universe. A person sitting in an observatory can point toward it from afar, but it is not possible for anyone to encompass the Muhammadan reality, because this reality is very far from human observation and perception. A human can point toward it from afar like a galaxy, but cannot speak about it in full.

I raise this point once again, and I am lost in thought over how great an honour the Muhammadan reality attained and embraced, and how his personality remained balanced, steadfast, and composed. After all, he was a human being. Whenever he praised one of his companions, that companion and his friends would be overjoyed, so much so that it was nearly fatal for them. Despite the fact that he was a human being, his Companions knew that he was human, and that he was a Prophet, and prophethood has a known sphere. A prophet is a human being, but the case of the Messenger ﷺ is different. The Lord of the universe is giving testimony in his favour. You know how great the Lord of the universe is, and if anyone does not know, the Muhammadan reality knows the greatness of the Lord of the universe very well. Yet despite this, he takes this great testimony with complete seriousness and does not allow any change in his conduct. This is true greatness, and this is the matter which is beyond every estimation.

Muhammad ﷺ alone reached this station, this station of greatness. This is the lofty peak of greatness and perfection which you alone have scaled. No other human has been able to reach this station, and it was the Muhammadan reality that became fit to bear this Messengership, which is a cosmic Messengership, an everlasting Messengership, and a universal human Messengership. This Messengership took form in his personality and was given to humanity in practical form. This final Messengership came in such a way that it kept moving in human form in Makkah and Madinah. These were Muhammad ﷺ. Fit for this station, and Allah alone knew who among His creation was fit for this station. Therefore He proclaimed:

﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous (standard of) character.﴾ (68:4) Allah Himself made this declaration, and proclaimed that Allah Himself sends blessings and peace upon Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. And this is the bounty of Allah alone, which He bestows upon whomever He wills. This is an elevated rank, and whoever receives it has received it.

Then there is another aspect to this testimony, which is the importance of morality within the human system from the Islamic point of view. In the Islamic system of life, good character is a fundamental element in every matter.

If you study the Islamic worldview or study the Seerah of the Final Prophet, you will see that the fundamental element in them is Islamic morality. The Islamic civilisational and legal system is established upon this moral element. In this system there is purity, cleanliness, trustworthiness, truthfulness, justice, compassion, goodness, fulfilment of promises, correspondence between word and deed, correspondence between intention and conscience, opposition to oppression and excess, prohibition of oppression and deceit, prohibition of consuming people's wealth by false means, prohibition of attacking people's honour, prohibition of committing obscenity and spreading obscenity, in whatever form it may be. And whatever legislation has been enacted in this system has been enacted to protect some one of these moral values, and through this legislation an effort has been made to instil moral values in people's conduct, their consciousness, and their behaviour. And these moral principles are observed simultaneously in individual, collective, and international conduct.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I was sent only to perfect noble character." You confined the purpose of your mission to moral purification. And a stream of hadith flows, urging: adopt good character and adopt a generous manner. Your blessed Seerah is an example of this, a clear page, and a lofty picture of noble character. And indeed you were deserving that the Creator of the universe should testify: ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous (standard of) character.﴾ (68:4) Just as the Messenger ﷺ is at the highest level of the tremendous character, so too the Islamic system of life that he presented possesses lofty moral values. Through this morality the settlements of the earth were joined to the heavens, the hearts of people were connected to God, and it was made clear what things Allah is pleased with.

This aspect is a distinguishing feature within the moral system of Islam, because Islamic morality is not the product of any society; it is not derived from earthly and material principles, nor is it derived from custom, tradition, honour, expediency, or mutual relations and ties. The foundation of these moral principles rests upon the pleasure of God. It rests upon the call: O people, rise towards Allah, cultivate within yourselves the praiseworthy attributes of Allah, so that the horizons of your humanity may join the heavens, so that you may find within yourselves the capacity to improve your life in the Hereafter. And that you may, with Allah...

﴿In a seat of truth, in the presence of a Sovereign, Omnipotent.﴾ (54:55) You become fit to sit "in a true assembly in the presence of an all-powerful King." Therefore Islamic morality is not confined within any material conception. It is boundless morality, and it lies at those ultimate heights to which no human can conceive of reaching, because this morality is based upon the following of the attributes of Allah, and is not derived from lowly material principles.

Furthermore, Islamic morality is not solitary morality. Truthfulness, trustworthiness, justice, mercy, and goodness are all moral qualities in which the mutual relation of more than one person is kept in view. These are morals connected with a system: mutual cooperation, mutual dealing, division of labour, distribution of rights, and matters relating to collective organisation. They are connected with a conception of life, and their source is the Divine Being. Therefore they are neither based on mysticism or personal permission, nor is their source material interests and worldly considerations; rather, the pleasure of Allah is their true source.

These moral principles were fully reflected in Muhammad ﷺ in their perfection, beauty, balance, straightforwardness, continuity, and stability, and because of this, the Messenger ﷺ was told:

﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous (standard of) character.﴾ (68:4) After this great praise, it is said that your future is extremely radiant. Tell the polytheists: wait for your evil end. You make accusations against the Possessor of great character; it is warned that the reality of your claims will soon become clear to you, as to who is the madman.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 68, verses 5–7:

"So you will see, and they will see, which of you is afflicted with madness. Surely your Lord knows best who has strayed from His path, and He knows best who are guided."

Al-maftun (86:6) means: the one who is misguided. Allah says that Allah knows both those who are guided and those who are misguided. Or its meaning is: the one who has been put into a trial and whose outcome is about to emerge. Both meanings are close to each other. In this promise there is reassurance for the Messenger of Allah and the believers, while for the opponents it is a warning. They had accused the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of madness (junun). By this madness they did not mean that his intellect had gone, since the actual situation was contradicting that. Rather, they meant that the influence of madness had come upon him, and in this their indication was towards the idea that every poet has a devil who inspires poetry to him. Indirectly they attributed this matter to the Prophet (ﷺ), whereas the teachings that the Prophet (ﷺ) presented had no connection with poetry or the talk of madness.

In this verse Allah the Exalted gives consolation that the future will reveal the reality of the Prophet (ﷺ) and also the reality of those who deny him. And it will become known which of the two is misguided. For further reassurance it is said that the Lord, the Exalted, knows who is misguided and who is on the right path. It is this speech that is being revealed by Him, so nothing is hidden from Him. Because of this, you would bear every excess of the enemies, and as a result of this your enemies would be disturbed, and because of your steadfastness there would arise anxiety and wavering within them, as comes in the following verses.

In the next verse, you are told that inwardly the condition of these people is very weak. Their thinking has become hollow from within. Outwardly they engage in hostility, they dispute, they deny the truth, they make all kinds of accusations against you, but inwardly wavering has arisen among them. They have been shaken, and regarding the beliefs on which they appear firmly fixed, in reality they themselves lack confidence in a large part of them. They are ready for bargaining; they want that you be a little flexible and they be a little flexible. But those who are to bring about an ideological revolution can bring it only when they stand firm upon their moral principles. These people are not very serious about the beliefs that they hold. They have grasped a few outward supports with which their interests are connected. Therefore, do not obey any of them.

﴿So do not obey those who deny.﴾ (86 : 8) ﴿They wish that you would compromise, so that they would compromise.﴾ (86 : 9) These people are not willing to bargain. Their wish is that a half-and-half deal be settled, the way merchants haggle over prices. But they know that ideology and trade are different. A person of conviction never agrees to bargain over his beliefs and ideals, because in matters of ideology even a small point is as precious as a big one. Indeed, in ideology there is no such thing as a small or a big point. An ideology is a complete whole. In it, no one obeys another, and no one gives up any part of his ideology.

There are countless narrations about the matters on which the polytheists of Makkah were ready to bargain with the Prophet (ﷺ). They proposed that if he showed some leniency, they would too. They asked that he stop speaking ill of their gods and stop saying that worshipping these idols was a foolish act. Or they proposed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accept some of their religion and they would accept some of his. In this way, they said, their honour would be preserved before the people of Arabia. This is the habit of all compromisers: they decide on a half-and-half basis. But the conduct of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was clear and firm. He neither compromised (mudahanat, meaning to yield or flatter in matters of principle) nor showed leniency. Yet apart from the principles of the religion of Islam, in all other matters he adopted a very gentle manner. He was excellent in dealings, very good-natured in social life, and treated people very well. As for matters of religion, they concerned God, and God's guidance was this:
﴿So do not obey those who deny.﴾ (86 : 8)

Therefore, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Makkah, even in such difficult circumstances, never made any bargain in matters of religion. He was in a very trying situation. His movement was under siege. He had a few companions. From every side they were being persecuted. They were snatched away and subjected to the most severe torture. Yet they endured patiently. However, they never refrained from reciting the declaration of Tawhid (the oneness of God) in front of the greatest tyrant. They did not do this to win over the hearts of the enemies, nor to escape their torment. They never let slip any truth that had even a distant connection with their faith.

Ibn Hisham, in his Sirah, narrates from Ibn Ishaq: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began to openly proclaim Islam and call his people to it, they did not respond to or refute his religion. But when he began to mention their gods and to call their worship foolish, they regarded this as a great crime and took great offence. They gathered against him and began hostility. Only those whom Allah had brought into Islam remained with him, but they were very few and weak. Abu Talib, the uncle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), supported him and defended him, standing before him as his protector. And the Messenger of Allah continued his work, speaking out at length, and no one could stop him from his words."

When the Quraysh realised that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not refrain from the things they disliked, and that their ranks had split, and that he continued to criticise their gods, and when they saw that their uncle was determined to support him and would not hand him over to the Quraysh, a delegation of the Quraysh's nobles went to Abu Talib. Among them were Utbah and Shaybah, the sons of Rabi'ah; Abu Sufyan ibn Harb ibn Umayyah; Abu al-Bakhtari al-As ibn Hisham; al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib ibn Asad; Abu Jahl (whose name was Abu al-Hakam Amr ibn Hisham); Walid ibn al-Mughirah; Nubayh and Munabbih, the sons of al-Hajjaj ibn Amir; and others who went with them. They said: "Abu Talib, your nephew has abused our gods, found fault with our religion, and called our beliefs foolish. He has declared our forefathers misguided. Now there are two paths before you: either stop him from these things, or step aside between us and him, because just as we do not accept his religion, you do not accept it either. We will deal with him."

Abu Talib spoke to them in very gentle words and sent them away courteously. They returned.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued his work. He proclaimed his religion and called people to it. But after this, the differences between him and the Quraysh became intense. The hostility went far, the people's fire of enmity grew hotter, and talk against him spread everywhere. People began to incite one another against him. They said: "Come on, against this man!"

These people went again to Abu Talib and said: "Abu Talib, you are the eldest among us, honourable and noble. We asked you to stop your nephew from this matter, but you did not stop him. By God, we cannot tolerate this situation, where he abuses our forefathers, calls our beliefs foolish and finds fault with our gods. Either you stop him, or you withdraw your support from him. Otherwise, there will be war between us and you, and whichever side is destroyed..." Or they said similar harsh things, and then left.

This dispute among his people weighed heavily on Abu Talib. He found the enmity of the whole people a burden. He also did not wish to hand over the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to them and bear the disgrace. Ibn Ishaq says: Ya'qub ibn Utbah ibn al-Mughirah ibn al-Akhnas told me that when the Quraysh spoke these words to Abu Talib, he summoned the Prophet (ﷺ). He said to him: "Nephew, your people came to me and said this and that. So have mercy on me and on yourself, and do not place upon me a burden I do not have the strength to bear."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) understood that perhaps Abu Talib's opinion on this matter had changed, that he too was about to abandon him, hand him over to the Quraysh, and that Abu Talib was now withdrawing his support and help. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Uncle! By God, if these people were to place the sun in my right hand and the moon in my left, and demand that I give up this work, it would not happen. I will continue this work until Allah makes this religion prevail, or until I am destroyed." It is said that the voice of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) broke, he wept, and he stood up and left. When he had gone, Abu Talib called out: "Nephew, come here!" When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned, Abu Talib said: "Go and do whatever you wish. By God, I will not hand you over to them at any price."

This is the picture of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): even at that time he was steadfast in his call, while his honoured uncle was thinking of withdrawing. Abu Talib was his supporter and protector, and he was the last fortress in which the Prophet could seek refuge against his enemies on this earth.

This was a very bright and powerful picture. By its nature and reality it was entirely unique. Its colour and reflection were all unique. Its expression and dialogues were also of their own kind: a picture of a very new and serious stance, shining as brightly as this belief shines, and containing within it the certification and the meaning of testimony.

﴿And indeed you are upon a magnificent character.﴾ (68 : 4)

Ibn Ishaq himself also narrates another picture of these lofty morals. He says: Yazid ibn Ishaq narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: I was told that Utbah ibn Rabi'ah was a chief. One day he was sitting in a gathering of the Quraysh, and he proposed, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting alone in the Masjid al-Haram: "Would it not be appropriate for me to speak with Muhammad (ﷺ) and put some matters before him? Perhaps he will accept them, so that we give him whatever he demands and he refrains from our gods." This was at the time when Hamzah had already accepted Islam and the Quraysh had seen that the number of the Prophet's supporters was increasing. They said: "Abu al-Walid, go and speak to him." Utbah got up, came, and sat down before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "Nephew, you know your standing among us. You have a very high rank and your lineage is very noble. But you have put your people into a great calamity. The community has been split. You have mocked our ideas, criticised our religion and gods, and called our forefathers unbelievers. Listen to me. I will put some proposals before you. I hope you will consider them, and perhaps you will accept some of them."

It is said that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Abu al-Walid, speak. I am listening." He said: "Nephew, if by the religion you bring you intend to gather a great deal of wealth, we will collect so much wealth for you that you will become the richest of us all. And if you want high status, we will make you our chief, and we will not decide any matter without you. If you want kingship, we accept you as our king. And if some affliction befalls you that you cannot repel, we will arrange a treatment for you, and we will spend whatever we can on it until you are healthy again. Sometimes it happens that something attaches itself to a person and he must seek a cure for it."

These and other such words he said. When Utbah had finished, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been listening to all of it. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Abu al-Walid, have you finished?" He said: "Yes." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Now listen to me." He said: "Yes, speak." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) began to recite:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 68, verses 10–13:

Now the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is commanded that he should not accept any word from one particular man among them, who is very eloquent in speech. Here the Qur'an, in its own distinctive manner, does not name him, but it enumerates all the base qualities that were found in this man. A threat is given to him with extreme humiliation and contempt:

﴿Do not obey one who swears much, a worthless man, who goes about slandering, who hinders good, who transgresses beyond bounds, who is sinful, cruel, and besides all this, of doubtful birth, because he has wealth and sons. When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "These are tales of the ancients." We will brand him upon the snout.﴾ (Qur'an 68:10–16)

Some narrations state that this man was al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, and concerning him the following verses of Surah al-Muddaththir were also revealed:

﴿Leave Me with the one whom I created alone, and to whom I granted abundant wealth, and sons present with him, and made everything smooth for him. Then he desires that I should give more. No! Indeed, he has been stubborn toward Our verses. I will impose upon him a difficult ascent. Indeed, he thought and deliberated. So may he be destroyed, how he deliberated! Then may he be destroyed, how he deliberated! Then he considered. Then he frowned and scowled. Then he turned back and was arrogant. And he said, "This is not but magic transmitted [from others]. This is not but the speech of a human being." I will drive him into Saqar.﴾ (Qur'an 74:11–26)

Many narrations report that this man was constantly engaged in conspiracies against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, used to frighten his companions, obstructed the path of the Islamic call, and day and night turned people away from the way of Allah. Some narrations also state that the verses of Surah al-Qalam refer to Unays ibn Shariq and al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. Both were fierce opponents of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; they were always at war with him and used to incite people against him.

This severe threatening statement, both in this surah and in other surahs revealed in this period, is proof that conditions at this time were very severe, and that this man, who was active against the Muslims and the Islamic movement, whether he was al-Walid or Unays (the first opinion is preferred), had a very great role in obstructing the Islamic movement. Moreover, from these critical verses it becomes clear that this man was of a very ill nature, and there was not a trace of goodness in his soul.

What kind of man he was: the Qur'an mentions nine of his qualities, and all of them are blameworthy:

1. Hallaf (68:10) (one who swears much). Those who swear many oaths are usually those who are not truthful; in their consciousness is the knowledge that people do not trust them and consider them liars. This man swears oaths, and by swearing many oaths he conceals his lies and thus gains people's trust.

2. Mahin (68:10) (worthless). Light in his own eyes, unreliable in the eyes of people. The need to swear many oaths arises for him precisely because he is light. He himself has no confidence in himself, and nor do people have confidence in him. Although outwardly he is wealthy and has a following, therefore a king, a rich man, and a strong and tyrannical person can also be light. This is because disgrace and honour are both psychological qualities; they never leave a human personality. A noble person is weighty, even if in other respects of the world he is not a great man.

3. Hammaz (68:11) (one who taunts). This man points out people's faults through words and gestures, both to their faces and behind their backs. Islam regards such a person very badly, one who finds fault with people. This is against courtesy, against high manners, and also against treating people with respect, whether they are great or small. The Qur'an has mentioned this quality in several places and has strictly forbidden it.

It is said in one place: "Woe to every slanderer and backbiter" (104:1). And elsewhere:

"O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people, perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women, perhaps they may be better than them. And do not defame one another, nor insult one another by nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith." (49:11). All of these are kinds of ill-temper and tale-bearing.

4. Mashsha'un bi-namim (68:11) (one who goes about spreading tales). He spreads among people words through which their hearts become sullied, relations are severed, and love ends. This is a base act, and light people do such things. No self-respecting person commits this kind of act while expecting people to look upon him favourably. Even those who listen to the words of such a person do not think well of him. In their hearts these people also consider him bad, and they say, "Would that this person had not told us this evil thing."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not like that he be told something by which his heart would become displeased with any of his companions. He would say: "Let no one convey to me anything about my companion, for I wish to come out to you with a heart that is clear towards you." (Abu Dawud and others)

In the Sahihayn it is reported: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by two graves and said: 'Both of them are being punished, and they are not being punished for a great sin. One of them did not protect himself from urine, and the other used to carry tales.'"

Imam Ahmad narrated the hadith of Hudhayfah: "The one who carries tales will not enter Paradise." (Ibn Majah)

Imam Ahmad narrated from Buraydah ibn al-Hasib: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Shall I tell you who among you is the best?" The Companions said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah!" "Those who, when they are seen, Allah is remembered." Then he said: "Shall I tell you who are the evil ones?" "Those who carry tales, who create enmity between friends, and who seek out faults in the innocent."

For Islam, condemnation of this kind of evil trait was very necessary, because this trait is blameworthy, base, and causes corruption in society, just as it creates discord between friends. And it was necessary to expose such a person before he could create corruption within the Islamic society, fill people's hearts with enmity toward one another, and before he could harm the security of society. Such people often harm innocent people.

5. Mannā'un lil-khayr (68:12) (one who hinders good). That is, he deprives himself of good and also deprives others of it. This man used to prevent people from faith, although faith is the fountainhead of good. It is well known about this man that he used to say to his children and family: "If any of you accepts the religion of Muhammad, I will never benefit him." And whomever he suspected of leaning towards the religion of Islam, he would threaten and frighten in this way. This is why the Qur'an recorded this act of his too, that he is one who hinders good.

6. Mu'tadin (68:12) (one who transgresses beyond bounds). He goes beyond truth and justice. This man would overstep against the Prophet ﷺ, oppress the Muslims, oppress his own family, and prevent them from guidance and the true religion. To oppress anyone is a very evil act, and it is strictly forbidden in the Qur'an and Sunnah. Islam wants the eradication of every form of oppression, even in eating and drinking:

"Eat of the good things We have provided you, and do not transgress beyond bounds" (20:81). Justice and moderation are the fundamental principle of Islam and the sign of Islam.

7. Atheem (68:12) (sinful). He commits evil deeds, as if the quality of sin has become attached to him. Thus he is a sinner, and he commits every kind of transgression. This quality is inseparable from him; it is as if his very temperament is such that he commits every evil.

8. Utull (68:13) (cruel). This is a word which, because of the variety of its pronunciation and meaning, gives several meanings; it conveys a comprehensive sense that several words cannot express. It may be said that 'utull' means hard and dry, that is, oppressive. It also means one who eats and drinks much, harsh, savage, and withholding, estranged from his blameworthy nature, and bad in dealings.

It is narrated from Abu al-Darda: "'Utull' is one with a big belly, of crooked character, who eats much, drinks much, hoards wealth, and is miserly and stingy." But in the word 'utull' all these meanings are manifest in its harsh sound. That is, a person who is ugly in appearance in every aspect of noble character.

9. Zanim (68:13) (of doubtful birth). This is the conclusion of the blameworthy qualities. These are the qualities of one of the enemies of Islam. The truth is that the enemies of Islam can only be such detestable people. A zanim is one who has attached himself to a people while not really being of them, or whose lineage among them is doubtful. Its meaning also includes one who is very well known among people for wickedness, baseness, and mischief; he too is called zanim. The second meaning is closer, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah fits it better, although the application of this word attaches to him a quality that makes him light among his people, while he is very boastful and considers himself great.

"We shall brand him on the snout" (68:16). Among the meanings of khurtum is that it refers to the edge of a pig's nose. Perhaps this is what is intended here. In Arabic, al-anf (the nose) is used for honour, as in "high-nosed" (one of lofty pride). Ghamm al-anf (the nose being covered with dust) is used in the sense of humiliation. It is said: warma anfuhu (his nose swelled), hamiya anfuhu (his nose became hot), meaning he became enraged. Al-anfa (self-respect) derives from this. To brand the snout means that he will be disgraced. It may mean that a mark will be placed upon it, as slaves were branded, or that his nose will be made like the snout of a pig.

The truth is that these verses fell upon Walid like a bomb, for he belonged to a people among whom even noble persons tried to avoid the satire of poets. Yet here the Creator of the heavens rained such stones upon him, in a manner for which there is no parallel. Then this satire was recorded in a scripture, each word of which is read and recited throughout the entire universe, and it is established in the whole universe and granted permanence.

This was the stoning from the Lord of Majesty upon that contemptible person who was an enemy of His religion and an enemy of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Messenger who possessed the magnificent character. Whoever this enemy of Islam may be, he deserved it.

In connection with the mention of wealth and children, and with the arrogance and aggressions of those who deny the truth, a story well known among them is alluded to here, and it was widely discussed among the common people. Allah warns of the punishment for ingratitude toward the blessings of God. Those who do not discharge the rights of others and who forbid good (mannā' lil-khayr, 68:12) are warned that this wealth and these children are in the hand of Allah. It is also a trial, just as the people of the garden were under trial. Everything has its end, and not everyone remains in one state.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 68, verses 17–18:

﴿Indeed, We have tested them...﴾ ................ ﴿...they would not make exception﴾

It is possible that this story was well known among the people of Makkah. However, the purpose here is that all the affairs of this world are in the hand of Divine power. Whoever here is prosperous or destitute, he is under the test of Allah. And this is the very aim and purpose of this story here.

From the characters of this story it is apparent that they are very simple-minded people of a very backward kind, like the simple-minded inhabitants of villages. They are not endowed with deep thoughts, and they speak in plain terms. In the period when these verses were being revealed, most of those addressed by the Qur'an were such simple people, who were hostile to Islam and denied it, but their minds were not complex, nor did they hold philosophical ideas. Most people were simple-minded and straightforward.

As far as the manner of narrating this story is concerned, it is an example of the Qur'anic style of expression. It contains things that appear suddenly in a story and increase the eagerness to read and to find out, and it also contains scenes of human plans and their failure, showing how a person makes efforts on his own, but what happens is only what God wills. And this story is related in such a way that it is as if the characters are doing all of this before our eyes. Just look at it in the words of the Qur'an itself.

Now we are before the people of the garden. This is a worldly garden, not the garden of the Hereafter. They decided about this garden at night. Generally, when the garden is harvested, in every society the needy also attend on that day and they too receive their share of the produce. And the same custom was followed regarding this garden. But the present owners who inherited this garden have devised a scheme to deprive the needy. The events now move forward.

﴿Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the owners of the garden, when they swore that they would surely harvest its fruit in the morning, and they did not make any exception﴾ (86 : 71–81). They resolved to pick the fruit of the garden at early dawn, but after this resolution they did not say "if Allah wills." Nor did they decide that they would leave something for the needy too, and on this they also swore that they would surely do so, and they settled the matter. And at night they made this wicked decision. The plot they devised remained in their hearts, and they did not realize what would happen to the garden in the darkness of night. They had not even imagined it. They went to sleep, but Allah does not sleep. Allah did what was contrary to their plan. And this happened as a punishment: instead of thanking for the blessing, they showed rebellion, and they decided to cut off the share of the needy and the poor, although that custom had been continuing before. This is a sudden calamity that comes to light at this stage. In the darkness of night, some shadows sent by the hand of Divine power move into action. The people are asleep.

It is possible that this story was well known among the people of Makkah. However, the purpose here is that all the affairs of this world are in the hand of Divine power. Whoever here is prosperous or destitute, he is under the test of Allah. And this is the very aim and purpose of this story here.

From the characters of this story it is apparent that they are very simple-minded people of a very backward kind, like the simple-minded inhabitants of villages. They are not endowed with deep thoughts, and they speak in plain terms. In the period when these verses were being revealed, most of those addressed by the Qur'an were such simple people, who were hostile to Islam and denied it, but their minds were not complex, nor did they hold philosophical ideas. Most people were simple-minded and straightforward.

As far as the manner of narrating this story is concerned, it is an example of the Qur'anic style of expression. It contains things that appear suddenly in a story and increase the eagerness to read and to find out, and it also contains scenes of human plans and their failure, showing how a person makes efforts on his own, but what happens is only what God wills. And this story is related in such a way that it is as if the characters are doing all of this before our eyes. Just look at it in the words of the Qur'an itself.

Now we are before the people of the garden. This is a worldly garden, not the garden of the Hereafter. They decided about this garden at night. Generally, when the garden is harvested, in every society the needy also attend on that day and they too receive their share of the produce. And the same custom was followed regarding this garden. But the present owners who inherited this garden have devised a scheme to deprive the needy. The events now move forward.

﴿Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the owners of the garden, when they swore that they would surely harvest its fruit in the morning, and they did not make any exception﴾ (86 : 71–81). They resolved to pick the fruit of the garden at early dawn, but after this resolution they did not say "if Allah wills." Nor did they decide that they would leave something for the needy too, and on this they also swore that they would surely do so, and they settled the matter. And at night they made this wicked decision. The plot they devised remained in their hearts, and they did not realize what would happen to the garden in the darkness of night. They had not even imagined it. They went to sleep, but Allah does not sleep. Allah did what was contrary to their plan. And this happened as a punishment: instead of thanking for the blessing, they showed rebellion, and they decided to cut off the share of the needy and the poor, although that custom had been continuing before. This is a sudden calamity that comes to light at this stage. In the darkness of night, some shadows sent by the hand of Divine power move into action. The people are asleep.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 68, verse 33:

﴿Such is the punishment.﴾ And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater; if only they knew it. Thus is the trial also in blessings. Therefore the people of Makkah ought to know this.

﴿Indeed, We have tried them as We tried the people of the garden.﴾ (68:17) Therefore they should look to see where their good lies. And they should also consider that the trial and punishment of this world are brief; their recompense comes.

﴿But the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew.﴾ (68:33)

Thus, before the Quraysh is placed a well-known incident from the very society of their own Bedouin past. It is told that this old event can be repeated. They should not use their wealth to oppress the religion of Islam, for otherwise Allah can destroy it. And a signal is given to the believers that the chiefs of the Quraysh, who have been given wealth, property, power and status, and who are misusing them, are in a severe trial. Very soon the results will come before them. And if they desist, it is better for them; if only they would come to their senses.

﴿But the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew.﴾ (68:33) As for those who fear and are watchful, for them are degrees [of rank].

"Verily, for the God-fearing there are Gardens of Bliss with their Lord."

This is the difference between the end of the two groups. This is also the difference between their conduct and their reality. Their paths are separate, so their ends are certainly separate as well.

Now, after this, the Qur'an engages them in a dialogue that is entirely comprehensible, and the themes preceding it in the surah have made it clear. Questions are put to them one after another, questions for which they have no answer. Therefore they are unable to respond, because the only answer to these questions is one that is bitter, and they can offer no answer other than that. For them in the Hereafter there is a frightening scene, and in this world there is a declaration of war against them by the Lord, the Exalted.

Between this dialogue and these challenges comes also a threat: that in the Hereafter there is punishment for them, but also that in this world war will be waged against them. Thus the dialogue gains heat and the challenge becomes forceful.

Accordingly, the people of Makkah are addressed in the manner of a challenge.

﴿Shall We then treat the submitters like the criminals?﴾ (68:35–36). This question concerns the people mentioned in the preceding verses who were criminals, and its answer is only one: the Muslimeen (the submitters) cannot be like the Mujrimeen (the criminals). The Muslimeen are those who bow before their Lord. They are never like those who commit crimes, whose attributes were described in the preceding verses and which apply to the people of Makkah. Reason also demands this. Justice also demands that the end of criminals and of the submitters not be of one kind. Accordingly, a second question is asked. This too is a question of rebuke.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 68, verse 36:

What is the matter with you? How do you judge? That is: what has happened to you, why is your reason not functioning? On what proofs do you base your decisions? What are your standards of good and evil? Because according to your scale, a Muslim and a criminal are equal... After this rebuke and these questioning interrogations, the Qur'an now adopts a mocking tone, as if these people are not even fit for serious discourse.

Do you have a book in which you read that for you there is surely whatever you choose for yourselves? (68:37–38)

This is a mockery of them: from which book have you brought this knowledge? For no standard of reason and justice can accept your judgment. The summary of your judgment is that the Muslims and the criminals have one and the same end. Then it would be a strange and ridiculous book which decides according to your desires and your preferences, so that whatever you wish, those very judgments are recorded in it. They are not based on truth and justice, nor are they based on any principle of what is reasonable and known.

If there is no Book, then will there be some covenant from Allah with you, extending to the Day of Resurrection? And through this covenant, your right would have been accepted, that you have authority over your own selves, and you may do whatever you wish. But there is no such thing; Allah has made no such covenant with anyone. On what basis do they make such claims, and what is their proof?

Ask them: which of them will stand surety for that? (68:40), that is, who among them is the one who signs such an agreement and guarantees its enforcement, that there exists with Allah such a covenant, one that remains workable and enforceable until the Day of Resurrection. This is the kind of humour, so eloquent and so pointed, that a sensible person, on hearing it, is reduced to shame, because he is confronted with a very plain and clear reality.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 68, verse 41:

﴿Or do they have partners (who have taken this responsibility upon themselves)? Then let them bring their partners, if they are truthful.﴾ (68:41)

These people associated many deities with Allah, but the Qur'an does not call them His partners; it calls them their partners. The Qur'an explains that Allah does not know of any partner of His. It issues a challenge: let them bring those whom they assume to be partners, so that they may be seen. But from where can they bring them?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 68, verse 42:

On the Day when the Shin (severe moment) will be laid bare, and they will be summoned to prostration, but they will not be able to prostrate. Their eyes will be downcast, and humiliation will cover them. They used to be called to prostration when they were healthy and whole, and they would refuse.

Thus these people stand before this scene of the Resurrection. It is as though the Resurrection has already taken place, and they are being called: "Bring forth your associates whom you used to claim." And in the knowledge of Allah this Day is truly present, for in the knowledge of Allah there is no past, present and future. Presenting the knowledge of Allah in this way has a profoundly deep effect, and it is the distinctive style of expression of the Holy Qur'an.

﴿Yawma yuksyafu 'an saq﴾ "The Day when the shin will be laid bare." This, in Arabic idiom, is used for severity and distress. That is, in a difficult moment a person rolls up his sleeves and lifts his trousers, and his shin is exposed. Generally a person does this in a difficult time, and at that time they will be invited to prostrate before Allah, and they will not be able to do so, because the time will have passed, or because of what is said elsewhere:

﴿Muhti'een...﴾ "Hurrying along with their heads raised" (Surah Ibrahim 14:43 is not cited here, but the sense is: they will be running with their heads lifted). Their state will be that their nerves and bodies will be stiff from fear, and they will be unable to prostrate involuntarily. It appears that they will be very frightened and distressed. Further, this will be their condition.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 68, verse 43:

"Their eyes will be lowered, humiliation will cover them" (70:44). Such will be the proud, those who considered themselves great, on that Day. Lowered gaze and abject condition: these two states are the recompense of their evil deeds. The warning given at the beginning of the surah, that We would brand its snout (68:16), points here to the fact that they will suffer deep disintegration and will be disgraced and humiliated.

They are in such circumstances, broken and shattered, that they are warned and reminded why they reached this state, because these people turned away from the truth and behaved arrogantly. And when they were sound and whole, and were called to prostrate in worship, they behaved arrogantly. Now, because of this, they are in this humiliating position, and they have left behind the transitory world. Today they are called, but they have no strength within them.

"When they were sound and whole, they were called to prostrate" (68:43), but they refused. And today they are called and wish to do so, but they have no power, or no opportunity. In such a state, another warning, one that shakes hearts, is given, while they are already in anguish and restlessness and are bewildered.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 68, verse 44:

فذرنی ............ الحدیث (86 : 55) "So leave Me alone with those who deny this discourse." They are finished. This is a terrifying threat from Allah, the Compeller, the Subduer, who is Strong and Mighty. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ is told: leave these worthless creatures who deny this great discourse; I Myself will deal with them. Who was it that denied? It is the same human being whose strength is less than that of an ant. Indeed, in relation to this entire universe, he is not even equal to a particle floating in the air. Against the power and majesty of Allah, the Compeller, the Subduer, what is man, poor creature that he is?

"Muhammad (ﷺ), leave them to Me. You and the believers should sit in ease and tranquility. This battle is with Me, it is because of My religion. These people are My enemies. I am taking their affair into My own hand; they will come to know. You should sit back in peace and tranquility." How terrifying a threat it is, and how firm an assurance it is, for those who at this time are in an extremely weak position. And this is not merely an assurance. Allah, the Compeller, the Subduer, makes clear what strategy will be adopted against them. They are indeed very weak and feeble.

سنستدرجھم ................ متین (54) (86 : 44-54) "We shall draw them on step by step, from where they do not know. I give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm." These deniers, and all the inhabitants of the earth, are too insignificant for Allah to devise any plan concerning them. Yet Allah frightens them with His powers, so that they do not invite the wrath of Allah, and so that, before time runs out, they set themselves right, and realise that this apparent well-being in which they live is itself a great victory, over which they are boasting. And that the respite given to them, in which they may commit oppression, rebel, turn away from the religion of Islam and adopt error, is in fact a plan for an even worse end. It is Allah's plan that these people should bear their burdens in full, and when they come on the Day of Resurrection they should be laden with sins and deserving of being cast into shame, reproach and punishment.

In the plan that Allah has devised, Allah also adopts an exceedingly just and merciful manner: He tells them in advance, although they are enemies of His religion and enemies of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so that they may reflect and, if they wish, come onto the right path.

Allah grants respite, but He does not leave the wrongdoers aimlessly like an unbridled camel. When He seizes the wrongdoers, none can escape His grip. Here Allah describes His method, His sunnah and His will, and tells the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to leave to Me those who deny this discourse, so that you may see how I bring them to their end. These people take pride in wealth, children and position and status; I give them respite. These very blessings will become the cause of their punishment. Thus the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is reassured, and they are left to walk into the mouth of punishment.

This manner of expression is extremely meaningful, frightening and wondrous.

فذرنی ................ الحدیث (86 : 44) "Leave Me alone with those who deny this discourse." Between Me and these fools a war has now begun, and Allah has always been at war with such people. Through this declaration Allah instils in the minds of the Muslims that in the struggle between faith and disbelief, between truth and falsehood, you are not the parties; one party is these fools and the other is Allah. The command of this battle is in Allah's own hand.

This is indeed the reality, although outwardly the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the noble Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) appear to play important roles in the struggle between truth and falsehood, their role too is part of the working of the Divine sunnah and the Divine decree. The Messenger of Allah and the Muslims were instruments in the hand of Allah's power; it was Allah who used them. He is Fa'alun lima yurid, who does what He wills, and causes to be done. It is Allah who Himself does the work.

When these verses were revealed, the Messenger ﷺ was in Makkah, in the early days of Makkah. The Muslims were very few in number and weak. Thus Allah filled their hearts with tranquility, and thus He terrified those who were deluded by their strength, wealth, position and children. After that, when the Messenger ﷺ went to Madinah, the outward circumstances changed. Allah willed that the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims should also have an outward role in this struggle. But the real truth Allah always stated in clear words: where He was weak in Makkah, and also in Madinah where outwardly they were successful and powerful. At Badr He said:

فلم تقتلوھم ................ سمیع علیم (8 : 71) "So it was not you who killed them, but Allah killed them; and when you threw, it was not you who threw, but Allah threw (and the hands of the believers were used in this work). This was so that Allah might bring the believers through a great trial successfully; indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing." This is so that the reality may settle in their hearts that the party in the battle is truly Allah, and that this battle is His battle, so that He may write a reward for them in this trial. As for the real battle, it belongs to Allah, and as for victory, Allah bestows it too; Allah can grant this victory even without the Muslims. As for those who take part in it, they are instruments in the hand of power. And the armies of Allah are not confined to the believers alone.

In any case, the Qur'anic verses have made this truth absolutely clear, whether the Muslims outwardly are weak or strong; and the system of Allah's decree and destiny is also in agreement with this. This is also what the sunnah of Allah and the will of Allah require. As for the Muslims and the Islamic armies, they are merely instruments and means.

This is the truth which settles the believer in both states, strength and weakness, provided his heart is sincere and he relies upon Allah in jihad, because in the battles of disbelief and Islam the strength of the Muslims is not decisive; rather, the help of Allah is decisive. Allah becomes the guarantor of victory. Even if the Muslims are weak, they achieve victory, because they have Allah's support. Yes, Allah gives respite to the enemies, lengthens their rope, and according to His will, wisdom, justice and mercy, defeats His enemies at the appropriate time.

Moreover, this is a truth before which the hearts of the enemies of Allah also tremble, whether the Muslims are in a state of weakness or a state of strength, because the enemy of Islam also knows that our confrontation is not with the Muslims but with God, the God who is saying to His Prophet:

فذرنی .................... الحدیث (86 : 44) "Leave Me alone and the one who denies this discourse." You step aside and leave this wretched one to Me; but the plan of Allah is firm and His snare is deceptive. They will become entangled in it in such a way that they will not even perceive it, even though they are powerful. The very power in which these people take pride, and because of which they are deluded, will be the cause of their defeat.

They cast lots so that one person would be removed to lighten the ship. The lot fell upon him. The people threw him into the sea. A fish swallowed him. At that time Jonah (peace be upon him) called upon Allah when he was in severe difficulty and near death. He was inside the belly of a fish in the sea. There were darknesses upon darknesses, and waves upon waves. Here he called out:

لا الہ الا انت سبحانک انی کنت من الظلمین ("There is no deity but You; glory be to You; indeed I was among the wrongdoers").

Then the grace and mercy of Allah reached him, and the fish, by the command of Allah, cast him onto the shore. At that time his condition had become such that he was left like a lump of flesh. The chemical action of the fish's stomach had made his skin soft, yet Allah kept him alive, miraculously, and Allah is not bound by the laws of life that He Himself created.

Here Allah says that had the grace and mercy of Allah not been there, the fish would have cast him out in a state in which he would have been blameworthy, that is, blameworthy in the sight of the Lord, because he had left his position of da'wah a little hastily. Allah accepted his glorification, accepted his acknowledgment and excuse, and showed mercy upon him.

﴿So his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous.﴾ (86:05)

This experience was presented to the Seal of the Prophets (ﷺ) so that he might benefit from it in discharging the duties of his prophethood. He was to carry out the final mission in the light of all earlier experiences. He was to reap the harvest of all advice, all lessons and all experiences, so that making decisions in his work would be easier for him and he could bear this burden well. Thus, in the coming age, even under the most modern conditions, the vehicle of life could be driven according to these principles, and when the future brought a new problem, its solution would be found within the principles of this call (da'wah) and mission.

The experience that Prophet Yunus (peace be upon him) passed through is placed before the Prophet (ﷺ). This is so in circumstances where people, like those of Yunus's time, have taken up obstinacy, denial and rebellion. This advice was given to him at a time when he was relieved of the responsibility of the battle between truth and falsehood. That responsibility was taken up by Allah. He will wage the battle as He wishes, and He will act at the time He wills. He gave him the command that he should continue his task, that is, conveying the message, with patience and steadfastness, whatever difficulties come in this path. All decisions will be made at their proper time. He should neither leave the station of da'wah nor be hasty.

Among the difficulties and hardships of the Islamic da'wah, the greatest hardship is patience, and waiting for the time when Allah issues His final decision. This is because the decision about the time of the da'wah's success rests with Allah, and He issues this decision according to His wisdom. Before the moment of that decision arrives, great hardships keep coming in this path. People deny, then they resort to persecution, they devise schemes and harbor intense enmity. Falsehood displays its strength and presents it inflated, just as air is blown into a balloon, and it appears frightening. People, overawed by apparent success and the movements of falsehood, follow it. Then the most difficult hardship is that the caller (da'i) must continue working firmly, with great steadfastness, perseverance and seriousness, and await the arrival of the promise of truth. He should have no doubt, and no hesitation should afflict him, while he is on the straight path, even if obstacles come along the way. Thus, waiting for the appointed time is itself a great hardship. As for the real battle, Allah has taken it into His own hands. He Himself is the party in this battle, and He is the one who is planning. He lengthens the rope for the wrongdoers, and wisdom lies hidden in this. This same promise was made to the Prophet (ﷺ) in those difficult circumstances, and later events confirmed it.

At the end, another scene of the disbelievers is brought here. These people would become extremely angry and seethe with rage when they heard the preaching and proclamation of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Intense enmity and envy would arise in their hearts, and this was expressed through their eyes. With poisonous and wrathful glances, these people stare at him. The Qur'an describes them with such eloquence that nothing can be added to it.

It was possible that these wrathful glances would have moved the feet of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), causing him to slip and waver. The rage, fury, malice, thirst for vengeance, envy and heat in their glances was described by the Noble Qur'an in a very beautiful manner. And along with these glances, they would also hurl abuse and accusations, saying:

﴿إِنَّهُ لَمَجْنُونٌ﴾ (68:51) "Indeed, he is a madman!" This is a scene that only the pen of Divine Power could inscribe. From it one can gauge the very difficult circumstances through which the call of Islam was passing in this early period. At that time the opponents in Makkah were a circle of influential criminals, a wide circle. Their hearts were burning and their eyes were splitting with rage. Yet Allah says how foolish these people are, that they are burning and seething in this small city of Makkah; this is in fact a universal program.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 68, verse 52:

وما ھوا ................ للعلمین (86 : 25) "Yet it is nothing but a reminder for the worlds." It is not for the people of Makkah alone. And how absurd is their accusation: do madmen present a program for global reform? True is Allah the Mighty, the Great!

It is appropriate here to discuss the word al-'Alamin (the worlds). At this stage the call is in Makkah, with only a few believers, the Messenger is being looked at with hostile eyes, and the polytheists of Makkah are using all their resources in the war against it. Yet even in this early period, in this difficult time, it is declared that this is a universal movement, just as it truly was. Therefore, when this movement adopted a universal character in Madinah, it was nothing new. Just as today the Western fabricators claim that the Islamic call adopted a universal character only after the success in Madinah.

The truth is that it was a universal call from the first day. This was Allah's intention, and in this way it will remain until the end of time. This is Allah's will. This call belongs to Allah, and He is its guardian. He is its supporter and helper. He is the one who fights on its behalf. The task of its bearers is only to remain steadfast upon it. He is the best of those who decide.
